observation_summary: The ConstructorInstantiator failed to instantiate inner classes because it only looked for a constructor matching the exact type of the outer class instance, failing when the constructor expected a supertype or when multiple constructors existed.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces a rigid, single-constructor lookup (which only checked for the exact class of the outer instance) with a more robust algorithm that iterates through all available constructors and validates parameter compatibility using `isInstance`. This is a procedural change to the instantiation logic, fitting the Algorithm/Method category.
evidence_used: The fix replaces 'withOuterClass' (which used 'getDeclaredConstructor(outerClassInstance.getClass())') with 'withParams' (which iterates through all constructors and checks parameter compatibility).
The new 'paramsMatch' method implements the logic to verify if the provided parameters match the constructor's parameter types.
The stack trace indicated a 'NoSuchMethodException' because the previous implementation was too restrictive in its constructor lookup.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes how the constructor is invoked, the root cause is the internal logic of the 'ConstructorInstantiator' class, not a mismatch in the API contract between two components.
The fix is a local procedural improvement to an existing instantiation mechanism, not the addition of a missing design-level capability.
